content.comment_body: Hello everyone, my location is UTC/GMT +3:30 hours and the current date and time is Friday, 27 January 2012, 18:30:59. My coordinates are Latitude 35° 42' North and Longitude 51° 25' East. On this date, sunset is at 17:26 and sunrise is at 07:08. I am unable to set up the astronomical clock with a custom time zone; I need help. I can configure all parameters except the time zone. My time zone is +3:30 hours and [product_name] does not offer this option.

Hello. Setting half-hour offsets in [product_name] is not possible. You may need to compromise for time zone settings. There was a previous discussion about this limitation before [article_no] was released. Alternatively, you can ask questions in the English forum as well.

Hello! Just select the closest time zone, GMT +3, in [product_name]. Then, correct the remaining 30 minutes difference by using a turn on/off delay of 30 minutes at the clock's output. (Translated with Google Translate as my English is not perfect)
This thread has been closed as the question was posted twice. A second topic about the Astronomical Clock is published within the same forum. Best regards, [user_name] Moderator

analysis.insight_summary: Users find that [product_name] does not allow setting half-hour time zones such as UTC+3:30, only whole-hour offsets. While other parameters can be set, the lack of support for half-hour increments restricts certain users, who must devise workarounds for accurate configuration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to allow time zones with half-hour increments so they can set up their local time zones accurately without needing a workaround.
